A.explanation: Green visible light has wavelength about $5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, which is much longer than X-rays at about $10^{-10} \text{ m}$.

B.explanation: In visible light red is the long wavelength end, so red light has a longer wavelength than green light.

C.explanation: Radio waves have wavelengths from about $10^{-1} \text{ m}$ upwards, which is greater than infra-red at about $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-3} \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: X-rays at about $10^{-11}$ to $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ are at much shorter wavelength than radio waves, so their range is less.

hints: List the electromagnetic spectrum in order of wavelength, starting from radio waves at the long wavelength end down to gamma rays at the short wavelength end.
Place infra-red, visible light with red to green to violet, and X-rays on that order and recall typical values such as $10^{-7} \text{ m}$ for light and $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ for X-rays.
Check each statement by comparing positions in that order, paying attention to whether it says shorter wavelength or smaller wavelength range.
walkthrough: Recall the order of decreasing wavelength: radio waves, microwaves, infra-red, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.

Note typical wavelengths: radio $> 10^{-1} \text{ m}$, infra-red about $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-3} \text{ m}$, visible about $4 \times 10^{-7}$ to $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ with red longer than green, X-rays about $10^{-11}$ to $10^{-8} \text{ m}$.
Green light is in the visible region so it is much longer than X-rays, and red light is longer than green light, so the first two comparisons are reversed.
Radio wavelengths are much larger than infra-red wavelengths, so the radio range is not less than the infra-red range.
X-ray wavelengths are many orders of magnitude smaller than radio wavelengths, so the wavelength range for X-rays is less than that for radio waves. This is option D.
